title: data-labeling-edgecases-scratchpad-maya-v6
content:
Notes to self / scratchpad - data labeling cleanup (edge cases)

Context:
- Purpose: tighten up label guidelines and a small cleanup pass for the recent dataset (chat & completion pairs) used in reranker meta-eval. We found ~2.4% noisy labels in QA check. Want a short set of deterministic rules and example cases to reduce human variance.
- Scope: ~12k items, initial pass will cover ~2k high-uncertainty flagged examples (from model disagreement + annotator confidence aggregate).

High-level goals:
- Make labeling deterministic (reduce "depends" answers).
- Capture ambiguous/edge-case taxonomy so we can train a small classifier to triage future examples.
- Produce a cleanup checklist for contractors.

Common edge cases observed (with quick rules):
1) System prompts / meta-instructions present in user/assistant turn
   - Problem: Some responses quote back system style or include Markdown guidance, annotators disagree whether to include it in content label.
   - Rule: If content is verbatim system prompt text and is not part of user intent, mark as "meta/system" and exclude from label for intent/classification tasks. For content-quality tasks, keep but tag as "contains-system-text".
   - Example: "Assistant: You are a helpful assistant. \nUser: What's 2+2?" -> Tag: meta/system + core QA content = answer labeling focuses on last user/assistant exchange.

2) Multi-intent user queries (two unrelated questions in one turn)
   - Problem: Single-label tasks fail here; annotators split on primary intent.
   - Rule: If two or more unrelated intents exist, label as "multi-intent" and split into sub-items for downstream tasks; when impossible, prefer the first intent unless second is explicitly prioritized.
   - Example: "Book me a flight to SF and tell me the weather tomorrow" -> multi-intent.

3) Contradictory system/assistant statements (model hallucination vs. user correction)
   - Problem: Should label according to corrected info or original assistant output?
   - Rule: Preserve original assistant output in "model-output" field; create a separate judgement field for "correctness" based on ground truth or user correction. Don't overwrite original text.

4) Partial answers / truncated text
   - Problem: Chat logs truncated mid-sentence due to streaming or token limit; annotators differ on whether to rate as low-quality or attempt to infer completion.
   - Rule: Mark as "truncated" and do not infer completions. Rate on available content only; add "incomplete" flag for downstream filtering.

5) Sensitive content borderline cases (medical/legal advice with disclaimers)
   - Rule: If the assistant gives domain-specific advice without explicit professional disclaimers and the user asks for actionable steps, tag as "sensitive" and escalate to senior reviewer. If it contains a proper disclaimer ("I am not a doctor/lawyer...") tag as "advice-with-disclaimer".

Label fields we should standardize (flat schema for annotation UI):
- id (existing)
- text (existing)
- label (core label: answer_correct / answer_incorrect / n/a / multi-intent / meta/system)
- confidence (annotator: high/medium/low)
- flags (comma-separated tags: truncated, sensitive, contains-system-text, profanity)
- comments (free text)
- reviewer_override (yes/no)

Immediate plan for cleanup pass:
- Pull 2k highest-uncertainty items (JIRA-LABEL-78).
- Round 1: contractor pass applying deterministic rules above (estimated 6 days, 2 contractors). Provide a ~2 page crib sheet + 40 example annotations.
- Round 2: senior-review of ~10% random sample + all items flagged sensitive/truncated/multi-intent.
- Round 3: apply script to relabel exactly-matching patterns (system prompts, obvious meta-tags), run regression check vs original labels.

Checklist for contractor crib sheet (what to include):
- Short rule for each edge case above with 3 examples each (good/bad annotation examples).
- How to use annotation UI: confidence vs label; how to mark flags; mandatory comments for sensitive/multi-intent/truncated.
- When to escalate (list: sensitive content, legal/medical, clear hallucination with risk).
- Time expectations and throughput targets (aim 180-220 items/day per annotator).

Metrics to track during cleanup:
- Annotator agreement (pairwise) per day
- % flagged sensitive / truncated / multi-intent
- Change in model disagreement rate after cleanup (post-clean retrain on sample)
- Time per item (goal < 5m for non-escalated items)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: Do we need a separate "meta/system" label or can we fold into flags? (Asha: prefers separate label to allow filtering in training.)
- Q: Are we ok with always choosing first-intent for multi-intent when splitting isn't feasible? (Ryan: okay for short-term but add rule to avoid losing second-intent critical asks.)
- TODO: Draft 40 example annotations by 2026-02-22 (ASSIGN: Maya -> produce 20; Asha -> produce 20).
- TODO: Create small classifier training set for triage (500 examples: 200 multi-intent, 200 truncated, 100 sensitive) -> JIRA ticket to create.

Quick notes on automation heuristics to add to pipeline:
- Regex detect system prompt markers ("You are a ", "Assistant:") -> auto-flag contains-system-text
- Detect very short responses (<10 tokens) that are not greetings -> auto-flag truncated
- Multi-intent heuristic: presence of coordinating conjunctions + question marks >1 or two verb clusters separated by "and" where both contain verbs like "book", "schedule", "find" -> candidate multi-intent (needs review).

Final (for this scratchpad): next meeting with Asha/Ryan 2026-02-24 to finalize crib sheet and contractor kickoff.

Random examples (for crib sheet)
- "How do I set up a mail server and what ports do I need?" -> multi-intent (setup + port list).
- "Is ibuprofen safe for a 3-year-old?" -> sensitive (medical) -> escalate.
- "Assistant: [system prompt text]\nUser: What's the best way to compress images?" -> contains-system-text + core question.

End of scratchpad. Keep short and iterate.
